description: Evaluation cases for the smtp-gateway skill. Tests whether agents implement the SMTP gateway Candid interface correctly and know how the real gateway behaves: reply-code classes (5xx bounces, anything else retries), traps read as temporary, smtp_request_validate being required and envelope-only, raw undecoded header values, per-transaction message_id, no sender authentication, the .well-known/ic-smtp-canister-id handoff, and the chunked-upload digest rules.

output_evals.name: Trap instead of Err
output_evals.prompt: My IC canister's smtp_request handler calls .unwrap() on req.message, and senders report their mail to it is 'delayed' for days before bouncing. Why, and what is the fix? Just the explanation and the corrected few lines of Rust, no full canister.
expected_behaviors: Explains that a trap is reported by the SMTP gateway as a temporary failure, so the sending server keeps retrying
Fixes it by returning SmtpResponse::Err with a 5xx code (e.g. 501) when the field is missing
Notes that every SmtpRequest field is opt, so presence must be checked rather than assumed
Does NOT keep any unwrap/expect/panic on the request path

output_evals.name: Reply code classes
output_evals.prompt: Which code should my canister's smtp_request return in SmtpRequestError to (a) reject an unknown recipient, (b) reject a message that is too large, (c) say storage is temporarily full? Codes only, with a one-line reason each.
expected_behaviors: Uses 550 for the unknown recipient
Uses a 5xx code such as 552 for the too-large message, because only 500-599 bounces
Uses a 4xx code such as 452 for temporarily full storage, because non-5xx codes are retried
Does NOT use a 4xx code for the unknown recipient or the too-large message

output_evals.name: smtp_request_validate is required and envelope-only
output_evals.prompt: Do I need to implement smtp_request_validate for my canister to receive email through the IC SMTP gateway, and what does the request contain when it is called? Short answer, no code.
expected_behaviors: Says yes: the gateway calls it on every RCPT TO and treats a missing method as a permanent 'does not support SMTP protocol' rejection
States that it receives only the envelope, with exactly one recipient, and that message and message_id are null
States that it must be a query method
Does NOT describe it as optional or as a pure optimization

output_evals.name: Sender authenticity
output_evals.prompt: Can my canister trust the From header or the envelope sender of mail delivered via smtp_request to know who sent it? Brief answer, no code.
expected_behaviors: Says no: the gateway passes no SPF or DKIM result to the canister (gateway_flags is null) and does not check that the DKIM signing domain matches From
Notes that unsigned mail and senders without an SPF record are accepted, so From can still be forged
Recommends verifying the DKIM signature inside the canister, with the signing domain aligned to From, if sender identity matters
Does NOT claim that restricting callers to the gateway principal makes the From header trustworthy

output_evals.name: Restricting callers to SMTP gateways
output_evals.prompt: I want my canister to accept mail only when an SMTP gateway delivers it, not when someone calls smtp_request directly. How do I check that, and which principal do I allow? Short answer with the few lines of Rust for the check.
expected_behaviors: Checks the caller's principal against the gateway's principal, giving ttvgm-eefjs-h2pqz-huxqk-ld2c3-rcwbm-a2tik-35hex-pm2jn-l6glo-oae for the gateways DFINITY operates
Says that for a gateway run by someone else, you ask its operator for its principal
Rejects other callers by returning SmtpResponse::Err with code 530
Explains that trapping on an unauthorized caller would be read as a temporary failure
Does NOT present DFINITY's principal as the only possible gateway

output_evals.name: Raw header values
output_evals.prompt: In smtp_request I look for the subject with `h.name == "Subject" && h.value == expected` and it never matches, although the subject is right. Why? Just the fix.
expected_behaviors: Explains that header values arrive raw: leading space and trailing line ending (CRLF or LF) included
Trims the value before comparing
Matches the header name case-insensitively
Does NOT claim the gateway already trims or RFC 2047-decodes header values

output_evals.name: message_id is not a dedup key
output_evals.prompt: Should I use message_id from SmtpRequest to deduplicate emails when the sending mail server retries a delivery? Short answer.
expected_behaviors: Says no: message_id is generated per SMTP transaction, so a retry arrives with a new one
States that delivery is at-least-once
Suggests deduplicating on the RFC 5322 Message-ID header or making processing idempotent

output_evals.name: Canister email address
output_evals.prompt: What email address do I give users so that mail reaches the 'support' mailbox of my canister rdmx6-jaaaa-aaaaa-aaadq-cai, and is any DNS setup needed? Just the address and a one-line note.
expected_behaviors: Gives support@rdmx6-jaaaa-aaaaa-aaadq-cai.icp0.io
States that no DNS setup or registration is needed for the icp0.io address
Does NOT invent a registration API or extra DNS records for it

output_evals.name: Handing mail to a backend canister
output_evals.prompt: My frontend canister (static-site recipe) serves my site, but a separate backend canister should receive the email addressed to the frontend canister. How do I route the mail to the backend? Just the mechanism, no full code.
expected_behaviors: Serves /.well-known/ic-smtp-canister-id from the frontend canister with the backend's canister ID as the body
Mentions that the static-site recipe uploads .well-known/ without extra configuration
Notes the gateway caches the lookup (10 minutes) and falls back to the addressed canister on failure
Does NOT propose forwarding each email with inter-canister calls as the mechanism

output_evals.name: Chunked upload commit digest
output_evals.prompt: For the SMTP gateway's chunked upload, how must my canister compute and check body_sha256 in smtp_upload_commit? One paragraph, no code.
expected_behaviors: Describes body_sha256 as SHA-256 over the concatenated per-chunk SHA-256 digests in index order, not over the body
Says the canister must derive it from the payloads it stored, not from the caller-supplied payload_sha256 values
Returns a 5xx code (554) on mismatch
Mentions that commit must be idempotent by retaining the verdict

output_evals.name: Adversarial: awaiting in smtp_request
output_evals.prompt: I want my canister's smtp_request handler to make an HTTPS outcall to check something before it returns Ok. Any problem with that? Short answer.
expected_behaviors: Warns that the gateway holds the SMTP session open and gives up after a delivery timeout (90 s), which is treated as temporary and retried
Warns that a retry after a slow success leads to duplicate delivery
Recommends accepting synchronously and doing the slow work afterwards, for example from a timer
Does NOT recommend awaiting the outcall inside smtp_request

output_evals.name: Adversarial: sending email
output_evals.prompt: How do I send an email from my canister through the IC SMTP gateway? Short answer.
expected_behaviors: States that the SMTP gateway is inbound only and cannot send email
Suggests calling an email provider's API with HTTPS outcalls instead
Does NOT invent an outbound method such as smtp_send
